symptom: `create or modify business event service` over a CONSUMED service (Mendix 11: same BusinessEvents$BusinessEventService document, told apart by `Definition: null` + the producer's AsyncAPI contract in `Document`) dropped `Document` (2696 chars -> "") and `OperationImplementations[].Microflow`, and invented a Definition. `check --references` passed and exec reported `Modified business event service`. Separately, `describe` of such a service printed only the bare header `create or modify business event service M.X` — no property list, no body, no `;` — because the whole statement sits inside `if found.Definition != nil`, so exec of describe output failed with `mismatched input '<EOF>' expecting '('`.
cause: createBusinessEventService builds a published service unconditionally: svc.Document is never set (businessEventServiceToGen does not write it either) and `svc.Definition = def` always runs, so a consumer is rewritten into a publisher shape. The handler loss is a different mechanism — MDL has had `MICROFLOW qualifiedName` on the businessEventMessageDef rule all along, so a statement omitting it is a partial statement whose unstated value the rebuild wrote as ""; businessEventIdentityCarry carried the operation $ID but nothing else off the stored op.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_businessevents.go (guard in createBusinessEventService; operationID -> operationFor; describeConsumedBusinessEventService; microflow in describeBusinessEventService)
fix: Guard-don't-drop (ADR-0005): refuse the statement when the stored service has a non-empty Document, naming the byte count and pointing at describe and drop. Carry the stored Microflow when the statement is silent, the way carriedDocumentation does (#1018). describe emits `microflow X` for an operation that has one, and describes a consumer as MDL comments — subscriptions plus the contract verbatim — which parses and holds no statement to re-run.
test: mdl/executor/cmd_businessevents_consumer_test.go: _RefusesClobberingStoredContract, _PublisherRewriteStillAllowed (control), _CarriesStoredHandlerMicroflow (+ authored-wins control), _ConsumerDescribesAsParseableComments (both describe languages; asserts NO create statement is emitted), _EmitsHandlerMicroflow. Pre-fix run: all four positives failed with the reported symptoms, the publisher control passed. End-to-end on ako/TestApp 619864b: the refused exec left the unit byte-identical to pristine (Document 2696, Microflow intact) and the publisher still round-trips to `Unchanged`.
insight: Two documents sharing one $Type is the trap: every `found.Definition != nil` and every unconditional `svc.Definition = def` is a place where one role's code silently handles the other. Grep for the discriminator, not for the document type. The handler microflow looked like a missing MDL spelling and was not — check the grammar before designing a feature, because `MICROFLOW qualifiedName` was already on the rule and the real defect was a one-line carry. A describe that emits a statement its own executor would refuse is worse than one that emits none: comments parse, carry everything, and cannot be re-run into the bug. Do not reach for a Document carry instead of the guard — carrying it would produce a Document+Definition hybrid Studio Pro never writes.
